\label{lemma-compose-homotopy}
Let $(A, \text{d})$ be a differential graded algebra.
Let $f, g : L \to M$ be homomorphisms of differential graded $A$-modules.
Suppose given further homomorphisms $a : K \to L$, and $c : M \to N$.
If $h : L \to M$ is an $A$-module map which defines a homotopy between
$f$ and $g$, then $c \circ h \circ a$ defines a homotopy between
$c \circ f \circ a$ and $c \circ g \circ a$.

stage_b_substantive_review_note: Independent source-first comparison against pinned, proof-masked dga.tex line 344: For a chain homotopy h between f and g, the equality d(h)=f−g is preserved under pre/post-composition by chain maps a,c, proving c h a is a homotopy between cfa and cga.

\label{lemma-homotopy-direct-sums}
Let $(A, \text{d})$ be a differential graded algebra.
The homotopy category $K(\text{Mod}_{(A, \text{d})})$
has direct sums and products.

stage_b_substantive_review_note: Independent source-first comparison against pinned, proof-masked dga.tex line 374: Arbitrary products and direct sums of dg modules descend to the homotopy category by componentwise homotopies and the universal properties of the constructions. Both exist as claimed.
